abstract: We study a duopoly model of behavior-based pricing in which consumers can either disclose or hide their data. We contrast two data policies. Under an open data policy, disclosed data is shared with all firms. In the unique equilibrium, all consumers disclose, and firms price discriminate, leading to welfare losses from inefficient poaching. Under an exclusive data policy, disclosed data is accessible only to the firm from which a consumer previously purchased. In the unique equilibrium, all consumers hide, prices are uniform, and the market is efficient. We test these contrasting predictions in an experiment. Under the open data treatment, subjects predominantly act as predicted but do not fully disclose. Under the exclusive data treatment, buyers initially excessively disclose as sellers reward loyalty, but shift toward hiding as sellers begin employing poaching strategies. The discrepancy between theoretical and observed privacy choices can be explained by the presence of consumers who, irrespective of the data policy, are committed to either disclosing or hiding their data.
abstract_zh: 我们研究了一个基于行为定价的双寡头模型，其中消费者可以选择披露或隐藏其数据。我们对比了两种数据政策。在开放数据政策下，披露的数据对所有企业共享。在唯一均衡中，所有消费者都选择披露，企业实施价格歧视，导致因低效挖角而产生的福利损失。在独家数据政策下，披露的数据仅对消费者之前购买过的企业可见。在唯一均衡中，所有消费者都选择隐藏，价格统一，市场效率高。我们通过实验检验了这些对比鲜明的预测。在开放数据处理下，受试者主要按预测行事，但并未完全披露。在独家数据处理下，买家最初因卖家奖励忠诚而过度披露，但随着卖家开始采用挖角策略，他们转向隐藏。理论与观察到的隐私选择之间的差异，可以通过存在一些消费者来解释，这些消费者无论数据政策如何，都坚定地选择披露或隐藏其数据。
title: We Value Your Privacy: Behavior‐Based Pricing Under Endogenous Privacy
title_zh: 内生隐私下的行为定价

abstract: One major barrier to small business investment is the close entanglement between corporate and owners’ personal assets, which ties corporate investment outcomes to their individual financial conditions. Personal bankruptcy pilot, by separating business from personal financial risks, may play a vital role in enhancing tolerance for failure and incentivizing corporate investment. We exploit the staggered implementation of personal bankruptcy pilot across Chinese cities and employ a multi-period difference-in-differences (DID) model to estimate causal effects on small business investment. The results show that personal bankruptcy pilot significantly boosts small business investment by enhancing firms’ optimistic expectations for the future and improving the financing environment. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that the investment-promoting effect is stronger for firms with heavier debt burdens and weaker access to mortgage loan; at the regional level, digital finance development and strong legal institutions amplify the policy’s effectiveness. Further analysis shows that personal bankruptcy pilot not only boosts investment but also improves investment efficiency and promotes firm scale. These findings underscore the importance of personal bankruptcy law in revitalizing small business.

title: Personal bankruptcy pilot and small business investment: evidence from China

abstract: This study tests the S-curve hypothesis in Korea’s trade with Vietnam using monthly data for 37 SITC commodity groups from 2000 to 2024. By extending recent asymmetric S-curve approaches to a disaggregated bilateral setting, we provide the first evidence of asymmetric S-curve dynamics for Korea–Vietnam trade. Using both symmetric and asymmetric cross-correlation analyses, we find that only a few sectors follow the textbook S-curve, while most show persistent positive or negative relationships. The asymmetric results reveal apparent directional differences: depreciations of the won often worsen trade balances in machinery and material manufactures through global value chain linkages, whereas appreciations tend to improve balances by reducing import costs. These findings demonstrate that exchange rate effects are asymmetric and sector-specific, underscoring the need for a calibrated policy approach.
title: Exchange rate dynamics and the S-curve in Korea–Vietnam trade: symmetric and asymmetric evidence
